# Session boot

This project's boot sequence is computed by vibe (the PROP-009 loading
model). To begin a session, read these files in order:

1. `spec/boot/STATIC.md` — if it exists. The static (priority) lane: read it
   first and in full.
2. `spec/boot/INDEX.md` — a generated TOML manifest. Read every file named
   by its `[[entry]]` tables, in the listed order. A `kind = "static"`
   entry is read directly; a `kind = "dynamic"` entry is an INCLUDE
   resolved at boot, and one carrying a `when` condition is read only when
   that condition holds for the current session.

Boot is pure file-reading — there is nothing to execute.

# vibevm-term — the terminal products of the vibevm umbrella

This repository holds the **closed-source GUI products** of the vibevm
umbrella, split out from the open-source host
([`vibevm`](https://github.com/vibevm/vibevm)) along the licensing axis —
**not** along the integration axis. The two integrate seamlessly: `vibe.exe`
(host) still spawns `vibeterm` / `vibeframe` / `vibe tree` when those are on
`PATH`.

## What lives here

The product packages live under `packages/org.vibevm.term/` (the
project-packages auto-discovery root, PROP-030 §3.3 — `vibe install` here
resolves them with no `[[registry]]` block):

- `packages/org.vibevm.term/common/` — **term-common**: shared TypeScript
  helpers (arg/keymap/packaging) and the normative contracts shared by all
  terminal products (the control protocol, the discovery file, the OSC 7773
  icon swap, env markers, the version-manager port).
- `packages/org.vibevm.term/launcher/` — **vibe-launcher**: the Rust GUI
  launchers (`vibetree` / `vibeterm` / `vibeframe` `.exe`).
- `packages/org.vibevm.term/vibeterm/` — **vibeterm**: the complex
  multi-tab terminal workspace (Electron + SolidJS).
- `packages/org.vibevm.term/vibeframe/` — **vibeframe**: the simple
  single-window terminal frame (VibeTree's host).

## Working in a package

Each package carries its own `vibe.toml`, `spec/` tree, `vibedeps/` (vendored
static deps — AI-Native Rust stack + redbook, populated by `vibe install`),
and `WAL.md`. To work in one, read its `spec/boot/INDEX.md` for the boot
sequence scoped to that package, plus the repo-root files you are reading
now.

The AI-Native Rust discipline is adopted from birth via `requires.packages`
(static-transitive) in every package's `vibe.toml`, mirroring
`packages/org.vibevm.fractality/` in the host repo. Inside this repo:
cells with single registration points and no sibling-cell coupling,
`scope!`/specmark-equivalent traceability to spec anchors, strict `tsconfig`
for the TypeScript code, branded types, `Result` errors, `vitest` cell tests.

## Cross-repo contracts

The specs in this repo cite host-side specs as `spec://vibevm/...` (e.g.
`spec://vibevm/common/PROP-019#root` for the Rust twin of the version-manager)
and mark each such cross-link `(host repo, cross-repo contract)`. The
terminal-product specs use short-form URIs scoped to this repo:
`spec://vibeterm/PROP-044#regions`, `spec://vibeframe/PROP-045#role`,
`spec://vibe-launcher/PROP-043#root`, `spec://term-common/PROP-vvm#root`.

## Commit discipline

Conventional Commits, atomic commits, no AI attribution — the same four
rules that bind every vibevm-umbrella repo. See the host's
[`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/vibevm/vibevm/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) for the
canonical statement.
